_asset_note: Placeholder symbol -- change to whatever stock you want to dry-run (any symbol Questrade can quote). Not investment advice; pick something liquid so quotes/candles behave normally.

fees._comment: Questrade's real equity commission is ~$0.01/share, min $4.95, max $9.95 PER TRADE -- not a clean percentage like Coinbase's maker/taker split. These rates approximate that for a trade around grid.tranche_size_usd ($3000): e.g. a $150 stock -> 20 shares x $0.01 = $0.20, but that hits the $4.95 minimum, so $4.95 / $3000 ~= 0.165%. If you change tranche_size_usd a lot, or trade a very cheap/expensive stock, re-check against Questrade's published commission schedule for your account and adjust these rates.

adaptations._comment: All OFF by default -- unlike the crypto grid bot, none of these have been backtested for equities yet. Turn them on deliberately (and ideally backtest first) rather than assuming the crypto-tuned values carry over.

execution._mode_options: dry_run = simulated price + simulated fills, no API calls that place orders. Only dry_run is implemented -- this is a Phase 1 build, same as the crypto grid bot.
execution._comment: Same fill model as the crypto grid bot -- see the main config.json for the full explanation. Quotes come from Questrade instead of Coinbase; see venue_questrade.py.

idle_yield._comment: Off by default. If you enable it, set apy_pct to whatever your actual Questrade cash/HISA rate is -- 4.5% was a reasonable USDC assumption for the crypto bot, not a Canadian-dollar cash rate.

notifications._comment: Same shape as the crypto bots' config -- env var GRID_BOT_DISCORD_WEBHOOK is reused if discord_webhook_url is null, so all four bots (grid, trend, grid_stock, trend_stock) can post to the same channel without re-entering the URL.
